notes:
— Vertical: payments platform (real-time fraud + in-chat agent).
— Primary ask: Dedicated GPU pool with throughput guarantees for peak windows (US region).
— Latency SLO targets: p95 <150ms for <256-token responses, p99 <400ms for longer pipelined flows.
— Throughput planning: target sustained 400–600 rps during business hours, 1,200 rps burst capacity during promos. Need guidance on reserved GPU sizing (estimating 6x A100-equivalents) and burst behavior.
— Autoscaling preferences: hybrid model — warm pool of pre-warmed GPUs (target 3–6 per AZ), reactive scale-up when queue length >120 and sustained for 30s, conservative scale-down with 15m cooldown. Warm pool warm-up target <= 90s (model load + kernel warming).
— Queueing behavior: want bounded queue with backpressure signal to app at 250 queued requests; prefer graceful degradation to lower-cost model variant rather than hard reject.
— Cost sensitivity: high — finance wants clear unit economics for reserved commit vs burst. Request Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching/quantization tradeoffs.
— Security: VPC/private deployment for transaction data, HSM/KMS integration required; retention controls for PII.
— PoC notes: observed cold-start spike up to 1.2s p95 when scaling from 0; warm pool eliminated that. Quantized 4-bit model reduced token cost by ~35% with small latency penalty at high seq lengths.
— Quote from VP Eng: "We cannot afford occasional 1s tails during checkout flows — need predictable SLOs + clear remedies."
— Legal: pushing for uptime credit threshold at 99.9% and explicit throughput guarantees per region.
— Internal concern: networking team flagged MTU/path MTU discovery issues for on-prem rack connectivity; needs validation.
— Helpful artifacts: perf logs (s3://galvanic-prod/poc/2024-11/perf-logs), trial billing sheet attached in drive proposal.
— Next: deliver updated SLA draft and warm-pool sizing proposal by 2024-11-25.
